result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both screenshots show only the first screen, and the two pages are nearly the same: a dark docs layout with section nav, a plain-language description, the install command in monospace and a horizontal rule before the Install section. Neither shows a usage example (dotenv-diff .env .env.example) above the fold. B adds a 'View on GitHub' button, but its heading wraps awkwardly and leaves '.env' alone on the second line; A's hero is more compact, though A also shows '. env' with a stray space. The flags table, exit codes and the lower part of the layout can't be seen in either image, so items 3 and 5 are scored conservatively, and no invented metrics, version numbers or testimonials are visible in either. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): The two pages are nearly identical lean, dark, single-column docs pages. Each has a clear tagline, the install command in the hero and nav links to Install, Usage, Options and Exit codes, with no invented stats. Neither shows a usage example on the first screen, and the screenshots stop before the flags and exit-code sections, so item 3 is scored on the nav links alone. B edges ahead because its hero is tighter, it puts the MIT license above the fold and its headline wraps more cleanly, while A's headline splits '.env' awkwardly across two lines.
